CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male presenting with complaints of bilateral knee pain. Over the weekend, he was moving boxes up and down basement stairs. By the end of the day, his knees were painful. He reports both knees are equally painful. He has had some knee problems in the past but attributes current pain to the repetition and weight of the boxes. He denies a specific injury. He has tried Tylenol and ice without significant relief. The pain was severe enough to keep him up Saturday night. He reports the pain affects his sleep but does not provide further details on impact to activities of daily living.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headaches.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant performed a few years ago for polycystic kidneys. Hypothyroidism. Arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications for kidney transplant. Synthroid for hypothyroidism, taking on schedule.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are stable with no fever. Heart rate and blood pressure are normal. Cardiac exam reveals 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, noted to be stable compared to prior exams. Right knee examination shows edema and erythema with pain to palpation and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears fine.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray shows good bony alignment with no acute fracture. White blood cell count is not elevated. Kidney function is very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute exacerbation of arthritis with right knee involvement. Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Patient advised to take it easy. Will consider further imaging and referral to physical therapy if symptoms continue. Hypothyroidism will be managed with continuation of Synthroid. Thyroid panel ordered. Arthritis management limited by kidney transplant precluding certain anti-inflammatory medications. Patient to be reassessed in a couple of weeks with consideration for physical therapy referral if needed.
